effect_estimate.comment: Combines headline intention-to-treat (ITT) estimates from both randomized experiments: null effect of face-to-face tenant engagement on payment (Table 4), large short-run increase in bill/loan payment from transparent disconnection-notice contract enforcement with no spillovers (Tables 5-6), null effects on 9-month compound water/sanitation connection, working supply, consumption, water spending, fetching time, and perceived fairness/quality because disconnected owners quickly reconnected via flexible payment plans (Table 7), and increased compound rental supply/income by landlords to cover utility bills without raising average tenant rent (Table 8).
effect_estimate.value: Tenant engagement RCT (N = 2,584 compounds): null effect on making >=1 payment within 1 month (ITT = -0.005, SE = 0.018, p = 0.776; control mean = 0.301) or 9 months (ITT = -0.002, SE = 0.019, p = 0.928; control mean = 0.558) and on total paid over 9 months (ITT = -US$ 0.575, SE = 2.011, p = 0.775; control mean = US$ 38.343). Contract enforcement / disconnection notice cluster-RCT (N = 1,001 compounds in 142 street clusters; 96 compounds [2.9% of 3,253] disconnected): increased likelihood of >=1 payment by 30.0 percentage points at 1 month (ITT = 0.300, SE = 0.039, p < 0.001; control mean = 0.110) and 19.5 percentage points at 9 months (ITT = 0.195, SE = 0.043, p < 0.001; control mean = 0.334); increased total amount paid by US$ 8.783 at 1 month (SE = 1.714, p < 0.001; control mean = US$ 5.026) and US$ 9.078 at 9 months (SE = 4.154, p = 0.031; control mean = US$ 24.722); and increased share of balance paid by 11.3 percentage points at 1 month (SE = 0.025, p < 0.001) and 7.8 percentage points at 9 months (SE = 0.027, p = 0.005), with no spillovers on untreated eligible compounds (1-month ITT = 0.010, SE = 0.023, p = 0.681, N = 996). At 9-month endline, enforcement had no statistically significant effect on compound piped water connection (ITT = -0.036, SE = 0.024, p = 0.135, N = 600; control mean = 0.916), working piped water connection (ITT = -0.033, SE = 0.041, p = 0.423, N = 591; control mean = 0.573), pour-flush toilet access (ITT = -0.014, SE = 0.019, p = 0.471, N = 608; control mean = 0.942), piped water as main source (ITT = 0.040, SE = 0.037, p = 0.286, N = 589), metered water consumption (ITT = 2.583, SE = 20.684, p = 0.901, N = 474), monthly water spending (ITT = US$ 0.664, SE = 1.005, p = 0.509, N = 334), or weekly fetching time (ITT = -17.569 min, SE = 21.682, p = 0.418, N = 601), while increasing the share of owners renting out compound space by 13.5 percentage points (ITT = 0.135, SE = 0.038, p < 0.001, N = 568) and monthly compound rental income by US$ 23.880 (SE = 10.127, p = 0.019, N = 525) without increasing tenant rent (ITT = -US$ 1.845, SE = 2.576, p = 0.474, N = 395).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Assigned 4 (Experimental evidence) because the study uses randomized controlled field experiments (appraised with RoB 2) that directly manipulate administrative/legal contract enforcement (targeted disconnection notices, hardship exemptions/payment plans, and physical disconnections/reconnections) and tenant accountability engagement, with strong baseline balance, full administrative billing follow-up, and direct measurement of compound water/sanitation connection and access outcomes.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines contractual service disconnection and low-cost reconnection for arrears (ENFORCEMENT: disconnection, reconnection, sanction); replacement of ad hoc de facto disconnection discretion with rule-based targeting alongside indigency/financial hardship exemptions, flexible payment plans, reconnection-fee waivers, and bill-dispute/complaint channels (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: discretion, hardship_exception, accommodation, complaint); subsidized last-mile connection fees/loans, consumption tariffs, and utility CDA/ICT payment guidance (BURDEN: fees, bureaucratic_assistance); property-owner contracting/account-holding rules, landlord-tenant tenure dynamics, and bottom-up tenant engagement/community activism (ELIGIBILITY: property, tenure; participation).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: The core contract enforcement intervention (the experiment testing contractual disconnection notices/disconnections and the sole experiment evaluated on endline water/sanitation access, welfare, and rental outcomes) used a two-stage cluster-randomized design across 147 street clusters (73 treatment vs. 74 pure control street clusters, with standard errors clustered at the street level), alongside a sequential compound-level randomized tenant-engagement experiment. Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant) matches the street-cluster randomization of the primary enforcement trial.

sample_size.comment: Reports multiple nested samples across baseline listing, administrative billing RCT arms, and endline surveys; baseline Kayole Soweto descriptive survey (2015/2016) also covered up to 3,327 property-owner billing records / 2,287 surveyed property owners (Table 1) and 4,178 tenant households (Table 2), plus a 2014-2018 panel of 587 households in one settlement (Section 3.1).
sample_size.value: 5,091 property-owner accounts across 6 informal settlements (August 2018 baseline phone listing); Engagement RCT: 2,584 compounds with tenants (1,292 treatment, 1,292 control); Contract enforcement cluster-RCT: 3,253 compounds across 147 street clusters in 4 settlements (73 treatment clusters with 1,584 accounts; 74 pure control clusters with 1,669 accounts), with main ITT sample of 1,001 disconnection-eligible compounds across 142 street clusters (327 assigned to treatment, 674 pure control; plus 322 within-cluster spillover controls [N = 996 in eligible spillover analysis; N = 1,930 in ineligible spillover analysis]); Endline follow-up survey (Aug-Oct 2019): up to 608 compounds/property owners and 403 tenants

study_design.comment: Combines five years of daily utility administrative billing records (2014-2019) with baseline listing (Aug-Sept 2018) and 9-month endline property-owner and tenant surveys (Aug-Oct 2019), estimating intention-to-treat (ITT) and within-cluster spillover (SNT) effects with settlement fixed effects.
study_design.value: Sequential randomized controlled field experiments: (1) an individually randomized controlled trial of face-to-face utility-tenant engagement among compounds in arrears with tenants, and (2) a two-stage cluster-randomized controlled trial (randomized first across street clusters and second across disconnection-eligible compounds within treated street clusters) of targeted service contract enforcement via disconnection notices, combining administrative billing data and follow-up property-owner and tenant surveys
